Stearns County: 1,524 people in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025
HUD counted 596 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Stearns County in 2025; 86% of the available vouchers were in use.
In Stearns County, 1,524 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 182 from 1,706 in 2024. Those people lived in 596 households.
HUD reported 671 Housing Choice Vouchers available in the county, and 86% of them were in use, down 2 percentage points from 88% in 2024.
HUD classified the heads of 51% of those households as racial or ethnic minorities. Households paid an average of $466 a month toward rent and utilities, up $12 from $454 in 2024, while their average annual household income was $18,974, down $128 from $19,102 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
In 2024, families who received Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. This average applies to families who obtained assistance, not applicants who were still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
